QF.id: AIFM Fee Structure and Fund Performance_36

question.text: Category I and Category II AIFs must be structured as ________ per SEBI AIF Regulations because their underlying investments are primarily illiquid.

answer.text: Listed closed-end funds with mandatory stock exchange listing

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook states that Category I and Category II AIFs need to be formed as close-ended funds because their investments are primarily illiquid, and that Category III schemes may be either open-ended or close-ended. The Trap: Option B (open-ended with monthly redemption) is inconsistent with illiquid underlying investments. Option C overstates the rule by adding a mandatory listing requirement that is not stated in the AIF illiquidity rationale. Option D (interval funds with quarterly liquidity) is a mutual-fund style structure not used here. Note: Source pages 171 and 494 directly support the close-ended requirement for Categories I and II and the flexibility allowed for Category III.
